subject: Plain-Word Digest #2: emails that survive dark mode
preheader: Why some emails turn into white-on-white puddles in Gmail, and what this newsletter does about it.

stories.title: The white-on-white problem, in one paragraph
paragraphs: When your phone switches to dark mode, some email apps quietly fix your colors for you. They might paint the background dark but forget your text was already a dark color - so your words vanish.

The fix is simple and a little stubborn: put an explicit background color and an explicit text color on almost every piece of your email. When you set the colors yourself, the app stops inventing them.

stories.title: Tables are the quiet workhorse
paragraphs: Modern web pages use fancy layout tools that email apps mostly ignore. That is not nostalgia - it is that the oldest, plainest building block, the table, is understood by literally every inbox on earth.

So this newsletter's template is built from tables with inline styles: one wide wrapper, one fixed 600-pixel-wide card, header band, story slots, a single callout, and the footer. It looks the same in Gmail as it does in Outlook.
If you ever forward this issue, it survives the trip. That, not cleverness, is the goal.
